articles.title: Liu overpowers Eala for HK Open crown
articles.excerpt: Claire Liu of the United States powered to victory at the Hong Kong Tennis Open on Sunday, dismantling Philippine sensation…
articles.fullText:
Claire Liu of the United States powered to victory at the Hong Kong Tennis Open on Sunday, dismantling Philippine sensation Alexandra Eala 6-3, 6-0 for her maiden tour-level singles title.

Liu, who entered the WTA 250 event ranked 102nd in the world, added the SAR trophy to a cabinet which already includes challenger-level titles she won in Paris in 2022 and in Barranquilla in September this year.

The pair found themselves locked in a fierce battle at Victoria Park early on, trading blistering shots to go level at 3-3 in the opening set.

After the second-seeded Eala received medical treatment on her right knee, Liu began to pull away convincingly, capitalising on costly errors from her opponent to claim the opener in 38 minutes while overcoming a strong show of support from Filipino fans in the crowd.

The second set proved to be a far more straightforward affair, with Liu breaking serves and wearing out a visibly shaken-up Eala to take the title in dominant fashion.

"This week in general has been really fun," Liu told reporters after her win.

"But it's also been mentally really tough... last tournament of the year, it's a really big push.

"I was just trying to take it one day at a time, and I found myself in the finals."

She also spoke about having to shake off nerves prior to the championship match.

"You really want to win no matter what," she added. "But I think I was just trying to make it like it's just one other match, and yeah, it worked out."

Defeat denied a second major career title for Eala, who was bidding to add to her historic triumph in Washington DC in August that saw her become the first Filipina player to reach and win a WTA 500 final.

Still, Eala spoke highly of the support shown to her in the SAR.

"The fans are amazing, and they add another dimension to my job and to my life that beforehand I could not even imagine," Eala said.

"Thanks to them I'm able to have such special experiences and create such amazing memories, so I'm super, super happy for their support."

In the doubles final, Japan’s Miyu Kato and Chinese Taipei’s Chan Hao-Ching claimed the title, beating Talia Gibson and Maddison Inglis of Australia 6-4, 6-4.
_____________________________
Last updated: 2026-11-08 HKT 21:01

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: New buildings body to recruit about 90 staff: Linn
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said the Building Maintenance Support and Services Council plans to recruit around 90 people in…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Development Bernadette Linn said the Building Maintenance Support and Services Council plans to recruit around 90 people in the initial phase.

The government announced the formation of the new body in the wake of the deadly Wang Fuk Court fire last year, and it aims to help homeowners with building maintenance and renovation works. The council will be set up by the end of the year, offering a paid service to handle tendering and evaluation on their behalf.

Speaking on a TV programme on Sunday, Linn said the new staff will include professionals, technical staff, as well as support and administrative personnel.

"We want to begin recruitment now so that new hires can be onboard as quickly as possible, and the goal is to have all these staff join in phases and be fully in place between the beginning and the middle of next year."

On whether to adopt the two-envelope approach for projects – which assesses the technical aspects and the price separately – the development minister said that could apply to more complex projects.

And she doesn't believe it would raise the price tag.

"The two-envelope system mainly depends on the weighting which is predetermined, and ultimately, quality is guaranteed, and it won't drive up prices as a result."

Linn noted that penalties and spot checks would be strengthened, and will not rule out the possibility of introducing a demerit points system in the future.

Separately, she said more than 1,000 training-related applications had been approved under the Construction Innovation and Technology Fund as of September.

The government established the fund in 2018, entrusting the Construction Industry Council to finance construction technology training programmes for companies and organisations.

Writing in a blog post, Linn said the total funding amount reached HK$50 million, benefiting more than 400 companies and organisations.

She noted that more than 4,500 people have enrolled in courses offered by the Construction Industry Council over the past three years.

The development chief stressed her bureau will continue to promote local training and drive the use of technology to raise overall construction productivity.

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: Springboks carry out demolition of Azzurri
articles.excerpt: South Africa picked up where they left off in the Nations Championship by dismantling injury-hit Italy 66-7 in Turin on…
articles.fullText:
South Africa picked up where they left off in the Nations Championship by dismantling injury-hit Italy 66-7 in Turin on Saturday to claim a fourth consecutive bonus-point victory.

A Springboks squad boasting more than 1,000 caps ran in nine tries at the Allianz Stadium.

The victory put the world champions alone on top of the Southern Hemisphere standings with a perfect 20 points and +140 points difference following big home wins against England, Scotland and Wales in July.

South Africa face France in Paris next Friday before a trip to Ireland as they look to claim a place in the inaugural Nations Championship final at Twickenham at the end of the month.

The Azzurri will hope to bounce back in their final two home games.

They face Argentina in Genoa next Saturday before welcoming Fiji to Udine on November 21.

In Cardiff, Wales beat Japan 28-21 on Saturday to claim their second win of the inaugural Nations Championship.

Wales entertain New Zealand next weekend eyeing an unlikely first victory over the All Blacks since 1953.

Eddie Jones's Japan have just one win from four fixtures in the tournament.

Meanwhile, in Edinburgh, Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu was left lamenting his side's ill-discipline following a 43-21 defeat by New Zealand at Murrayfield.

Ewan Ashman became the first Scotland player to score a hat-trick of tries against New Zealand, the hooker's treble coming before half-time to give the hosts hope of a first win in this fixture.

The All Blacks only led 24-21 at the break but Scotland failed to score a point in a second half where Tuipulotu was sent to the sin-bin. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: Arsenal extend lead as Forest topple Man City
articles.excerpt: Manchester City suffered a third consecutive Premier League defeat at the hands of Nottingham Forest on Saturday, allowing Arsenal to…
articles.fullText:
Manchester City suffered a third consecutive Premier League defeat at the hands of Nottingham Forest on Saturday, allowing Arsenal to stretch their lead at the top of the table to six points.

Enzo Maresca's men desperately needed a victory at the City Ground to keep pace with the in-form champions, who have taken 27 points from a possible 30, but lost 3-1.

City had a mountain to climb after finding themselves 2-0 down in the 18th minute following goals from defender Jair Cunha and forward Liam Delap.

The visitors were much improved after the break and Rayan Cherki cut the deficit with an emphatic strike into the roof of the net.

But Delap restored Forest's two-goal advantage in the 73rd minute, rifling home with his left foot past the outstretched hand of Gianluigi Donnarumma to earn his side breathing room.

Forest manager Oliver Glasner sprinted down the touchline to celebrate with his team, who had not managed to score a single Premier League goal at home before Saturday.

City, who won their first seven league games under new manager Maresca, know that even if they close the gap to Arsenal, it might ultimately all be in vain.

The Etihad club are still waiting to discover their fate after being found guilty of more than 100 breaches of Premier League financial rules — with a huge points deduction one potential punishment.

Earlier, Arsenal made hard work of beating struggling Hull to underline their title credentials on the eve of the international break.

Captain Martin Odegaard finally broke the deadlock for the champions and title favourites in the 72nd minute.

Arsenal, who bossed possession at the Emirates, had a claim for a penalty in the closing minutes of the first half after Kai Havertz had his shirt pulled by Nobel Mendy.

But VAR ruled that the German forward was in an offside position in the build-up.

Frustration mounted as the second half unfolded, but Odegaard came to Arsenal's rescue, scoring his first goal since early September with a poacher's finish.

Noni Madueke cut in from the right before unleashing a left-footed shot that Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis spilled and Odegaard fired home from close range.

Arsenal manager Arteta praised his players but wants them to be more clinical after they recorded a third 1-0 win in four league games.

"We can still be much better, and we will improve in many phases, and we will get certain relationships to a different level that will be even more efficient," he said.

"That's the next step, to have bigger margins and when we have them, the opportunities, put them away to make sure that we don't have to hang in there the last few minutes."

In the early kick-off, Leeds struck in the 79th minute through substitute Noah Okafor to end Tottenham's three-match winning run.

The major talking point in the first half was a challenge by Leeds defender Jayden Bogle on Spurs winger Mathys Tel, which was reviewed for a potential red card by VAR officials before eventually being cleared.

Tel had to leave the field shortly before half-time.

Spurs boss Roberto De Zerbi, disappointed by his team's second-half showing, refused to be drawn on the incident, which was not reviewed on the pitchside monitor by referee John Brooks.

"In the first situation of Mathys Tel I didn't see, I can't say nothing," he told TNT Sports after the 1-0 defeat.

He added: "I have big confidence in the referee. Nothing changes if he goes to watch the clip or not. I think there was the VAR and if they didn't take the right decision, I don't know, but we have confidence."

Elsewhere, Jacob Murphy put Newcastle on course for a much-needed win with a spectacular strike in the 80th minute at Craven Cottage but substitute Rodrigo Muniz levelled just three minutes later to earn a 1-1 draw.

Forest's win against City means Michael Carrick's Manchester United will kick off against Aston Villa on Sunday in the relegation zone. (AFP)

Edited by Tony Sabine

articles.title: $10 meals fight social isolation
articles.excerpt: For many elderly residents and caregivers navigating the daily challenges of isolation and limited mobility, preparing a hot, nutritious meal…
articles.fullText:
For many elderly residents and caregivers navigating the daily challenges of isolation and limited mobility, preparing a hot, nutritious meal can feel like an insurmountable hurdle.

But at Shek Pai Wan Estate in Southern District, a novel community dining initiative is providing a vital lifeline, transforming a local children and youth services centre into a hub of warmth, nutrition and connection.

Run by the Aberdeen Kai-fong Welfare Association since March, the Community Dining Hall offers meals for just $10, enticing caregivers and vulnerable residents to make the trip to the centre.

“Everyone gets a good meal. That is wonderful,” said resident Leung Wah-fuk, adding that the no-MSG dishes are both delicious and healthy, which is vital for the elderly.

Fellow resident Leung Wai-chun echoed that sentiment, noting that the support is a genuine blessing for those who find it difficult to walk to the market or manage cooking alone.

Real impact
While filling daily nutritional needs is crucial, the programme’s true impact lies in its power to forge connections and spot individuals who might otherwise slip through the cracks.

Aberdeen Kai-fong Welfare Association Chief Executive Nora Ng emphasised that the target users are high-risk or hidden groups, including elderly residents living alone, caregivers, and families looking after children with special needs.

“Providing hot meals is not our main focus,” Miss Ng said. “Reaching out to high-risk or hidden groups is our main objective.”

Smart resources
This outreach-first philosophy is underpinned by smart resource allocation. Principal Assistant Secretary for Labour & Welfare (Children) Kevin Li explained that the project optimises the use of integrated children and youth services centres during their non-peak hours.

“We leverage the rich social welfare experience and manpower resources of social welfare organisations," Mr Li said.

He added that since these non-governmental organisations historically provide a wide spectrum of services - from rehabilitation to family assistance - they can quickly redeploy their resources to provide appropriate follow-up support for those identified through the dining initiative, embodying the policy goals of early identification, early intervention and sustained support.

Citywide vision
Since its launch, the pilot scheme has yielded positive results, having served more than 4,000 meals, reached nearly 400 hidden or high-risk individuals, and completed close to 350 case assessments.

Mr Li said that the programme serves as a model that effectively reduces social isolation while seamlessly catching those with hidden welfare needs.

What began as a local pilot is now blossoming into a citywide vision, newly backed by the Policy Address. Moving forward, the Government will reach out to integrated children and youth services centres across Hong Kong to invite them to join the initiative, ensuring that more isolated households feel valued, supported and truly seen.

articles.title: China icebreakers set off for Antarctica
articles.excerpt: China held a departure ceremony in Sanya, Hainan, on Saturday to mark the start of its 43rd Antarctic scientific expedition…
articles.fullText:
China held a departure ceremony in Sanya, Hainan, on Saturday to mark the start of its 43rd Antarctic scientific expedition.

Organized by the Ministry of Natural Resources, the mission will upgrade China's polar research stations and logistics network and carry out comprehensive, multidisciplinary surveys and monitoring in Antarctica.

It will also pursue priority research at the frontiers of polar science, test and apply domestically developed equipment, and deepen bilateral and multilateral cooperation in science and logistics support.

The expedition is supported by the icebreakers Xuelong and Xuelong 2, along with another vessel.

More than 600 team members from over 100 domestic institutions are participating, and the team is expected to return home in April. (Xinhua)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: France's Gehri, Russia's Isakova win HK triathlon leg
articles.excerpt: France’s Nils Serre Gehri produced a dramatic late surge to win the men’s individual title at the World Triathlon Cup…
articles.fullText:
France’s Nils Serre Gehri produced a dramatic late surge to win the men’s individual title at the World Triathlon Cup Hong Kong on Saturday, while Russia’s Diana Isakova continued her strong run of form by claiming the women’s race.

Gehri, who won the U23 title in Pontevedra, Spain, in September, clocked 50 minutes and 14 seconds.

He overtook Australia’s Callum McClusky right at the finish line to seal the victory, with Spain’s David Castro Fajardo rounding out the podium in third.

Hong Kong, China’s Nicholas Tsang finished 58th in 54 minutes and 44 seconds.

In the women’s race, Isakova arrived in Hong Kong fresh from a World Cup win in Rome and made it back-to-back victories, finishing in 55 minutes and 39 seconds.

Luxembourg’s Jeanne Lehair took second, followed by Huang Anqi of the national team.

Hilda Choi was the top finisher among Hong Kong triathletes in 37th place, with Cade Wright 39th and Bailee Brown 50th.

The roughly 24-kilometre course began along the Central and Wan Chai waterfront, with athletes opening with a 750-metre swim in Victoria Harbour.

They then tackled an 18.5-kilometre bike leg past Expo Drive, the International Finance Centre and the Central Piers before closing with a five-kilometre run to the finish line on Lung Wo Road.

The mixed team relay is scheduled for Sunday.

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: He Lifeng in video talk with Bessent amid Cuba row
articles.excerpt: Vice-Premier He Lifeng, who is leading China's economic and trade affair talks with the United States, held a video call…
articles.fullText:
Vice-Premier He Lifeng, who is leading China's economic and trade affair talks with the United States, held a video call on Friday with Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Trade Representative Jamieson Greer.

The two sides held candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges on implementing the important consensus reached between the two heads of state at their meetings in Beijing and Washington and the outcomes of economic and trade consultations, and on key economic and trade issues of mutual concern.

The Chinese side expressed serious concern over recent US economic and trade restrictions against China.

Both sides agreed that under the strategic guidance of the two heads of state, they would further leverage the China-US economic and trade consultation mechanism, continuously strengthen cooperation and properly manage differences so as to promote the stable and positive development of bilateral economic and trade relations, and contribute to building a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity.

News of the video call came as the Ministry of Commerce said on Saturday that China firmly opposes US unilateral sanctions on Chinese enterprises as the move violates international law and the basic norms of international relations.

A spokesperson for the ministry made the remarks in response to a media query that the US Department of State had announced sanctions on two Chinese enterprises and that this was reportedly the first time the United States has imposed sanctions on Chinese companies over so-called Cuba-related reasons.

In recent days, the ministry official said, the US side has escalated sanctions and suppression against China and introduced multiple discriminatory restrictions, which have seriously harmed the rights and interests of Chinese enterprises, deviated from the important consensus reached by the two heads of state, and undermined the stability of China-US economic and trade relations.

China urges the US side to correct its wrongdoings as soon as possible, the official said, noting that China reserves the right to take necessary measures to safeguard its legitimate rights and interests. (Xinhua)

Edited by Azam Khan

articles.title: Everton in fifth heaven in comeback win over Coventry
articles.excerpt: David Moyes said Thierno Barry had proved his point after the Everton striker's double inspired a 3-1 win against Coventry…
articles.fullText:
David Moyes said Thierno Barry had proved his point after the Everton striker's double inspired a 3-1 win against Coventry on Friday.

Moyes's side trailed to Yann Gboho's goal early in the second half at the Hill Dickinson Stadium.

But Barry proved too hot for Coventry to handle, netting twice in the space of just five minutes to turn the game in Everton's favour.

Barry has already reached 10 goals this season, surpassing his total for the entire 2025-26 campaign.

That miserable first season with Everton following his move from Villarreal is quickly becoming a distant memory of the in-form 24-year-old, who has six goals in his last seven appearances in all competitions.

"We gave away a really poor goal but the reaction from there was really good. Important that Thierno Barry got another couple of goals tonight which was huge for us," Moyes said.

"He can smile at me now and say I told you so and that's good. We always liked him and we want him to keep scoring."

Barry had been known for squandering chances that seemed impossible to miss last season, but he has been far more clinical this term.

"He's missed quite a few chances but tonight he got important goals for us," Moyes said after he equalled Harry Catterick's Everton record 592 games in charge.

"He's becoming an important piece for us and he's got 10 goals for us which is really good."

Among Premier League players, only Manchester City striker Erling Haaland has scored more goals than Barry in all competitions this season.

"I'm very happy because I'm a fan of him. I watch a lot of videos of him and try and do the things he does," Barry said.

"If I can stay with him until the end to get the Golden Boot I will try."

Everton are up to fifth place following their third successive win in all competitions.

"We got a performance and we got a result but I have to say Coventry made it really difficult for us. In the end we got the goals which mattered," Moyes said.

Coventry boss Frank Lampard was left frustrated with a pair of rejected penalty appeals that could have turned the match in his side's favour.

Lampard, who managed Everton from January 2022 to January 2023, said: "Big decisions affected the game, clearly.

"VAR looked at them. The James Tarkowski hair pull on Caleb Yirenkyi, then Vitaliy Mykolenko on Taiwo Awoniyi, I think he gets contact on the edge of the box which is a penalty.

"The second goal for them comes off the player's hand. If you're going to check the angles, there is an angle where it flicks in off his hand. VAR looked at it and decided not.

"The last touch to score is off the hand, in my opinion. I've seen a conclusive angle so I can disagree." (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

A Pakistani astronaut will join the Shenzhou-24 crewed flight mission as a payload specialist, the China Manned Space Agency said on Saturday.

After completing a short on-orbit flight, the Pakistani astronaut will return to Earth aboard the Shenzhou-23 spacecraft.

The mission will mark the first joint flight involving Chinese and foreign astronauts in the history of China's manned space programme.

articles.title: North Korean orphans fast tracked into state care to stem declining birth rate
articles.excerpt: Orphanages are now supplied more regularly after shift toward birth-friendly policies.
articles.fullText:
Read a version of this story in Korean
North Korea is attempting to address its decreasing birth rate by improving the conditions of state-run orphanages while increasing crackdowns on illegal abortions, residents in the country told Radio Free Asia.
The total fertility rate for North Korea is estimated to be 1.59 children per woman of childbearing age according to key statistical indicators from South Korea’s Ministry of Data and Statistics. This is well below the replacement fertility rate of 2.1 required to maintain the population.
The rate may be even lower than estimated, a 2025 report by the Washington-based Stimson Center’s 38 North project said.
Orphanages and nurseries were previously poorly supplied, meaning that taking in more children was difficult, but government policies have improved the situation, with supplies of milk, food, clothing and shoes flowing in more regularly, the residents said.
School children arrive to pay their respects before the statues of late North Korean leaders Kim Il Sung and Kim Jong Il at Mansu Hill in Pyongyang on Sept. 9, 2023.
(Kim Won Jin/AFP) “Recently, authorities have been more quickly sending orphaned children or children born to unmarried women to nurseries or orphanages,” a resident of the country’s northeastern province of North Hamgyong, who requested anonymity for security reasons, told RFA. “The residents’ reaction to this is generally positive.”
The resident talked about a situation where an unmarried woman from Kyongwon county, on the border with China, had to give up her child because of the difficulty raising it alone. The child was quickly accepted into an orphanage in October.
Though the resident did not specify how long it took to place the child, another resident, from nearby South Hamgyong province, told RFA that in another case, in the coastal city of Tanchon, it took about a month.
“In September, in Tanchon, a 6-year-old child became an orphan after his mother, who had been raising him alone, died of illness,” the South Hamgyong resident said on condition of anonymity to speak freely. The child “went to an orphanage after about a month.”
Supplies meeting demand
The government’s apparent priority on supplying nurseries and orphanages has come after a series of child-friendly policies were enacted including the Childcare Law of 2022 and the Law on Preferential Treatment for Multi-Child Families of 2025. Authorities actively encourage childbirth and child-rearing, including by pushing propaganda messaging that “having many babies is patriotism.”
A woman receives the "Communist Mother's Honor Award" during the Fifth National Mothers' Convention in Pyongyang, North Korea, Dec. 4, 2023.
(KCNA via KNS/AFP) The country’s leader Kim Jong Un famously was brought to tears in 2023 when he publicly discussed the declining birth rate at the National Mothers’ Conference in December 2023.
“Putting our efforts into raising the birth rate together with mothers is a critical revolutionary undertaking that cannot be resolved by the power of our Party and government alone,” he said at the event.
Sources in RFA reports after that incident explained that women were reluctant to marry and have kids because they wanted to focus on their own happiness.
Abortion crackdown
Another way the government has been trying to prevent a declining birth rate is to punish doctors who perform abortions .
By law, abortion is illegal in North Korea, but in practice, some doctors accept payment to perform the procedure in secret.
But these days, those doctors are harder to find, the North Hamgyong resident said.
“There are women who come home pregnant after serving in the military, and they try to get rid of the baby quickly before it is seen by others,” the North Hamgyong resident said. “But recently, abortion procedures have not been easy, so many end up giving birth.”
Unwanted pregnancies happen often in North Korea because sex education is non-existent, the North Hamgyong resident said. But even if the mother gives birth, administrative hurdles and societal pressure make it very difficult to raise the child. This is because it is impossible to register the child without the father, and because of the stigma surrounding unwed mothers.
Many unwed mothers are finding creative ways to put their children born out of wedlock in orphanages without having any official record of the birth, the South Hamgyong resident said. “In late September in Tanchon, a resident found a baby wrapped in a sling in a neighborhood alley and took it to the community center.”
Students attend class in North Korea, April 2, 2018.
(KCNA via Reuters) However, it was later revealed that the person who took the child to the community center was actually the maternal uncle of the woman who had given birth, the South Hamgyong resident said. Since the fact that the unmarried woman had given birth might become a major obstacle to marriage if known to the outside world, the uncle had resorted to a workaround for his niece.
The South Hamgyong resident said that the woman did not intend to become pregnant, and had tried to get an abortion but she could not find any doctor willing to provide one.
Edited by Yi Yongin in Korean and Eugene Whong in English.

articles.title: Ferrari boss lays down law to Hamilton, Leclerc
articles.excerpt: Ferrari team chief Fred Vasseur on Friday said both of his quarrelling drivers had been reminded that the Italian team…
articles.fullText:
Ferrari team chief Fred Vasseur on Friday said both of his quarrelling drivers had been reminded that the Italian team always comes first following a meeting at Interlagos.

Speaking to reporters at a scheduled news conference following opening practice at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix, Vasseur confirmed that he met seven-time champion Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc to discuss their clash and performance in Mexico last Sunday.

"The guidelines are always the same," said Vasseur. "They are two competitors with a fighting spirit for sure, but they need to have respect for each other.

"But mainly, and firstly, they need to respect the brand, the team, the people working at home, the people working on track. I think we are putting a lot of effort on this and the message was clear -- and will stay clear."

Hamilton, who started from his first pole for the team, had made clear after the Mexican race that he felt Leclerc had been over-aggressive on the opening lap when they tangled and ran off track, wrecking Ferrari's hopes of victory.

The British driver called for serious discussions and confirmed on Thursday that he remained frustrated and would not stop speaking his mind on the issues.

The drivers had not met since the Mexico event as Leclerc returned to Monaco for the birth of his first child.

Vasseur deflected claims, from Hamilton and others, that Leclerc races harder against his team-mates than others by citing his aggressive pass of four-time champion Max Verstappen of Red Bull in Texas.

"If you have a look at what Charles did in Austin in the first sector, everybody said it was magic," he said. "The line is fine between the two, but he didn't crash into the other car."

Vasseur added: "For sure, in this situation, we failed collectively because we were one and two and we didn't win the race at the end. That means that it's clear that we failed and we have to react.

"But the conclusion of the meeting yesterday (Thursday) evening was a clear reminder that the Ferrari is coming first, is coming first for the brand, for the employees, for the Tifosi, and this we have to keep it in mind."

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: US markets close mixed as tech stocks push back
articles.excerpt: US technology stocks bounced back on Friday from their worst drubbing in more than a year, but the Nasdaq Composite…
articles.fullText:
US technology stocks bounced back on Friday from their worst drubbing in more than a year, but the Nasdaq Composite Index posted a fourth consecutive weekly decline as investors sifted for clues about what comes next in the AI trade.

Gains within technology were broadly shared, with the semiconductor index rallying and Nvidia, Advanced Micro Devices and Sandisk rebounding.

The broad revival underscores investor faith in the AI buildout that has driven US stock indexes to dozens of record closes this year, despite a shakeout that began with a US long-term Treasury yield spike in August and the stock volatility of the past month.

“We still think AI is the dominant theme in this bull market,” said Keith Lerner, chief investment officer at Trust Advisory Services in Atlanta. “We are still giving technology the benefit of the doubt.”

The S&P 500 climbed 24.70 points, or 0.34 percent to end the session at 7,378.43. The Nasdaq gained 264.42 points, or 1.09 percent, to 24,579.42, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average declined 237.33 points, or 0.46 percent, to 51,285.73.

Lerner said he views the selloff this week, which has taken the Nasdaq into correction territory denoting a 10 percent decline from its peak a month ago, as likely offering a longer-term buying opportunity for many investors.

“AI has gone on trial several times in this cycle and come away with an innocent verdict,” said Adam Turnquist, chief cross-asset strategist for LPL Financial in Charlotte, North Carolina. Referring to the US midterm election results that spurred heavy selling in AI stocks, he said, “This week we saw a little bit of a knee-jerk reaction.”

US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1 percent, suggesting the labour market remained resilient. Traders added to bets that the Federal Reserve could hike rates as soon as next month, with a 78 percent chance of a December move compared with a 70 percent chance seen earlier, according to LSEG.

"Those are strong numbers,” said Joe Saluzzi, co-head of equity trading at Themis Trading in Chatham, New Jersey. But he asked, “Will the Fed want to raise interest rates in the face of a market which is teetering?"

Tesla and SpaceX were among technology shares bouncing back from Thursday’s plunge. Among other stock movers, software firm Atlassian dropped after reporting first-quarter results. Airbnb climbed after the vacation rental platform raised its full-year 2026 revenue growth forecast.

Oil prices were slightly lower, adding to bullish sentiment for riskier assets, and were on track for sharp weekly declines. The S&P 500 energy index was on track for a double-digit weekly percentage drop. (Reuters)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: HK rebuts 10-nation statement
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today expressed strong dissatisfaction with and firm opposition to a so-called joint statement…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government today expressed strong dissatisfaction with and firm opposition to a so-called joint statement issued by ten countries, namely the United States, the United Kingdom, France, Germany, Japan, Italy, Australia, Canada, the Netherlands, and New Zealand in relation to the sentencing in the “conspiracy to commit collusion” case of Wong Chi-fung, which deliberately distorted facts and smeared the Hong Kong SAR.

The Government pointed out that the statement disregards facts, blatantly interferes with its judicial power and power of independent adjudication exercised in accordance with the law, and maliciously smears the Law of the People’s Republic of China on Safeguarding National Security in the city (the Hong Kong National Security Law (HKNSL)).

It strongly urges the countries concerned to immediately cease interfering in Hong Kong matters, which are purely China’s internal affairs.

The Government stated that Hong Kong is a society underpinned by the rule of law and has been consistently fulfilling its constitutional duty to safeguard national security in accordance with the law, upholding the principles that laws must be observed and strictly enforced to bring offenders to account.

Wong Chi-fung pleaded guilty to the charge of “conspiracy to commit collusion with foreign countries or with external elements to endanger national security” under the HKNSL. The court, acting in strict accordance with the law and judicial procedures, based on objective facts and sufficient evidence, has delivered a sentence independently and impartially, fully manifesting the spirit of the rule of law in Hong Kong.

The Government stressed that everyone is equal before the law. Regardless of their political stance, background or status, anyone who breaks the law must be held legally accountable. Attempting to distort criminal judgments handed down in accordance with the law into actions targeting “political expression” or “political participation” is purely political manipulation deliberately intended to confuse the public and distort right and wrong.

It pointed out that the rights and freedoms enjoyed by Hong Kong residents in accordance with the law are fully protected by the Constitution, the Basic Law, and the HKNSL, among others. However, all rights and freedoms must be exercised within the legal framework and cannot be used as a pretext for engaging in acts that endanger national security.

It is each and every sovereign state’s inherent right to enact laws safeguarding national security. Not only is this in accordance with international law and international relations based on the Charter of the United Nations, but is also an international practice. Many Western countries, including the UK and the US, maintain extensive and strict national security legal frameworks, and will absolutely not allow their citizens to collude with external forces to endanger their own national security.

There are numerous cases in the countries concerned where their own citizens as well as foreign nationals have been prosecuted on charges such as “foreign agent” and “foreign interference”, not to mention instances of arbitrary arrest and malicious prosecution. The groundless attacks by the countries concerned on Hong Kong’s rule of law and judicial system, or their attempts to interfere with the city's work in safeguarding national security in accordance with the law through political pressure, only demonstrate their hypocritical double standards, which are utterly ugly and despicable.

The Government urges the countries concerned to stop making irresponsible and misleading remarks, and to cease interfering in any form in the operation of judicial proceedings of the HKSAR and Hong Kong affairs, which are purely China’s internal affairs. Any attempt to shake the determination of the Hong Kong SAR Government to safeguard national security is bound to be in vain and will never succeed.

articles.title: Summit connects 3,300 youth
articles.excerpt: ​The Home & Youth Affairs Bureau today hosted the third edition of the Youth Development Summit - Hong Kong …
articles.fullText:
​The Home & Youth Affairs Bureau today hosted the third edition of the Youth Development Summit - Hong Kong .

Under the theme “Pioneering New Horizons, Venturing into the Future”, the summit gathered officials responsible for youth policies from various regions, alongside experts and leaders of different sectors as guest speakers.

The event attracted over 3,300 young people registered to participate, including over 700 from the Chinese Mainland and 35 overseas countries such as the United States, Laos, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Nigeria and Rwanda, enabling them to exchange views and engage in mutual learning on issues of concern to young people.

Chief Executive John Lee said in his opening remarks that the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government will actively take forward youth development initiatives under Hong Kong's Five-Year Plan, enhance youth development opportunities, and nurture a new generation of young people with an affection for the country and Hong Kong, who are empowered with a global perspective as well as an ambitious and positive mindset.

He added that the Government will continue to expand young people’s international exposure through exchanges, internships and learning experiences, and will work with schools and different sectors of the community to cultivate an environment where young people can unleash their potential and shine on the global stage.

At the session on “Shaping the Future with Youth” held this morning, Secretary for Home & Youth Affairs Alice Mak delivered a keynote speech and shared the vision of the city under Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan in enhancing youth development opportunities, and supporting young people in pursuing their dreams. She highlighted key Government measures and initiatives on youth development that foster a conducive environment for local young people to thrive, and to unleash their full potential.

She noted that the Government would continue to develop the Youth Development Summit as a flagship brand, convening young minds from around the world for exchange year after year. She encouraged young people to step into the new horizons and become the backbone of our long-term economic and social development, and the driving force that will shape our future.

Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki officiated at the summit and delivered opening remarks. He also hosted a welcome dinner yesterday for officials, guests, and speakers from the Chinese Mainland and overseas visiting Hong Kong for the summit.

articles.title: More new jobs added in US as unemployment eases
articles.excerpt: US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1 percent, suggesting the labour…
articles.fullText:
US nonfarm payrolls increased more than expected in October and the unemployment rate fell to 4.1 percent, suggesting the labour market remained resilient and giving the Federal Reserve more scope to focus on inflation stemming from the Middle East conflict.

Payrolls jumped by 165,000 jobs last month after an upwardly revised 60,000 gain in September, the US Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics said on Friday.

Economists polled by Reuters had forecast payrolls advancing 65,000 after a previously reported 29,000 increase in September.

Estimates ranged from 35,000 to 125,000 jobs.

Economists estimated the economy needed to create at least 40,000 jobs per month to keep up with growth in the working-age population. The so-called breakeven rate has declined from roughly 150,000 in 2024 because of the smaller labour force.

The unemployment rate declined from 4.2 percent in September.

Historically low layoffs and a recent jump in job openings have raised the prospect of labour market tightening.

But economists and US central bank officials have maintained that the labour market poses no inflation risk. Some economists have argued that a shrinking supply of workers amid an immigration crackdown and retirements is the primary driver of the relatively low unemployment rate.

Meanwhile, Canada's unemployment rate went up to a six-month high in October and the economy lost a few thousand jobs as the private sector and full-time employment saw declines, data showed on Friday.

The unemployment rate edged up to 6.7 percent in October from 6.5 percent in the prior month, Statistics Canada said. The last time it was higher than this level was 6.9 percent jobless rate in April.

The economy lost a net of 4,700 jobs in the month, taking the total size of the jobs the economy lost this year to 46,000 overall.

The October report highlights a continued weakness in the labour market in Canada that has failed to post any job gains on average this year as trade tensions between the US and Canada worsened and businesses hunkered down to save costs. (Reuters)

Edited by Edmond Fong

articles.title: The Download: a humanoid cleans house and Samsung builds for the AI boom

articles.fullText:
This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology.

I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.

—Grace Huckins

When I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning service in San Francisco, I immediately signed up for the waitlist. I wanted my apartment to feel like The Jetsons , even if just for an hour.

The device that arrived at my building belongs to Tau Robotics, a local startup. Its long-term goal is to make autonomous cleaning robots a reality, but the technology isn’t quite there yet. For now, humans pilot the robots remotely, watching them work through onboard cameras.

There were some unexpected challenges along the way, but also moments that felt like a glimpse of the future.

Find out how well the machine cleaned my home—and how close we are to truly autonomous domestic robots .

A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub

Generative AI models depend on stacks of specialized memory chips. To meet soaring demand, Samsung is building a vast new semiconductor manufacturing campus in Pyeongtaek, South Korea.

I visited the sprawling campus south of Seoul, where three fabs already operate around the clock, a fourth is coming online, and thousands of workers are racing to build a fifth.

Step inside the vast chipmaking complex powering the AI boom .

—Michelle Kim

This story is from the Impossible edition of our print magazine. Subscribe now to get every issue as soon as it lands.

The must-reads

I’ve combed the internet to find you today’s most fun/important/scary/fascinating stories about technology.

The Nasdaq suffered its worst day since April 2025 amid fears of an AI slowdown. ( CNN )
+ The Magnificent Seven lost over $1 trillion. ( WSJ $)
+ Tesla and SpaceX lost over $420 billion combined. ( CNBC )
+ Wall Street’s AI sell-off has spread to Asia and Europe. ( WP $)
+ The AI stock bubble may finally be bursting. ( FT $)
+ What even is the AI bubble? ( MIT Technology Review )

2 Emboldened Democrats are lining up to rein in Big Tech
They’re preparing to haul tech CEOs before Congress. ( Verge )
+ Bernie Sanders wants a national data center moratorium. ( Quartz )
+ Yassamin Ansari plans to pause advanced AI development. ( CNBC )
+ The backlash could delay Anthropic’s IPO. ( Reuters $)
+ No one wants a data center in their backyard. ( MIT Technology Review )

3 The US has warned of an “ongoing cyber threat” to fridges
A spate of hacks has hit commercial freezers. ( Reuters $)
+ Russia has denied claims it’s behind the attacks. ( Politico )

4 AI is helping Anthropic’s models improve nearly twice as fast
Researchers say Claude is speeding up its successors.( Information $)
+ But recursive self-improvement will take time. ( MIT Technology Review )

6 Covid vaccines’ economic benefits may be double what we thought

7 The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is changing the ocean’s color 
The infamous debris has brightened the water. ( Scientific American )

8 NASA has unveiled a mysterious new experimental aircraft
The X-70 is expected to take flight within two years. ( Ars Technica )

9 Elon Musk has signaled the end for the Cybertruck
Tesla is winding down production in Texas next year. ( FT $)
+ It was one of last year’s biggest tech flops. ( MIT Technology Review )

10 Three-hour movies have sent viewers rushing to a pee break app
7,000 RunPee users signed up for You Can See Everything . ( WSJ $)

Quote of the day

“The steamroller showed up today.”

—Jim Carroll, a senior wealth adviser at Ballast Rock Private Wealth, tells Reuters how investors feel as the AI trade unravels and $2.5 trillion is wiped off tech stocks.

One more thing

EMILY NAJERA

How a couple of ski bums built the internet’s best weather app

The best snow-forecasting app for skiers isn’t a federally-funded service or a big-name brand. It’s OpenSnow, a startup that uses government data, its own AI models, and decades of alpine-life experience to deliver the best predictions out there.

The app proved especially vital last winter, one of the weirdest on record. It even made microcelebrities of its forecasters, who sift through reams of data to write “Daily Snow” reports for locations around the world.

We headed to the Tahoe mountains to hear how two broke skiers created the best weather app on the slopes .

—Rachel Levin

We can still have nice things

A place for comfort, fun, and distraction to brighten up your day. (Got any ideas? Drop me a line .)

+ The US has a new national park: Arizona’s otherworldly Chiricahua .
+ Fancy living in a flying saucer? A rare 1960s Futuro house is on the market.
+ Don’t Cook That collects real recipes from old cookbooks that you should absolutely not make.

articles.title: I watched a humanoid robot clean my apartment. It felt like a taste of the future.
articles.excerpt: I’m not the sort of person who typically pays for a house cleaner. I’m too frugal, and I kind of…
articles.fullText:
I’m not the sort of person who typically pays for a house cleaner. I’m too frugal, and I kind of enjoy putting on a podcast and going to town on my tub with a Magic Eraser. But when I saw an X post about a new humanoid-robot cleaning service in San Francisco, I immediately signed up for the waitlist. I wanted my apartment to feel like The Jetsons , even if just for an hour.

I was also motivated by journalistic interest. In order to ensure an authentic experience, I didn’t tell Tau Robotics, the startup behind the X post, that I was a journalist—though I did use my real name, so it’s possible someone looked me up. Tau’s long-term goal is to make autonomous cleaning robots a reality, but they’re not quite there yet: For now, the robots are piloted remotely by humans, who watch what’s going on via cameras mounted in the robots’ heads and wrists. As the robots clean, they collect data that Tau will use to train up their more independent descendants. Every counter successfully wiped and T-shirt successfully folded will help the models that power the robots learn to do better on the next go-round.

Because this data is so valuable to Tau, the company charges less for cleaning than one might expect for such a cutting-edge product. At the time I booked, Tau was offering $30 for an hourlong cleaning with a single robot; now the charge is $60 per weekly cleaning with two robots, or $100 for a one-time visit. But even at the cheaper rate of $30 per hour, Tau’s robots aren’t a great bargain. They are thorough but slow, so if you, like me, are tempted to stand around watching them for their entire visit, it would probably be a better use of your time to just take care of the cleaning yourself.

But the robots are physically capable of cleaning, and they’re undeniably cute. Tau has armed each four-and-a-half-foot-tall robot with a 3D-printed “head” with antennae that allow it to communicate with Tau’s headquarters, as well as two 3D-printed claw “hands” (the more humanlike alternatives apparently aren’t durable enough, and claws do surprisingly well for most cleaning tasks). Mine was wearing a Tau Robotics shirt, and grippy socks so that it didn’t scratch hardwood floors.

With all the human support they need, the robots are closer to radio-controlled cars than Waymos. Many tasks, such as making the bed and folding laundry, require what’s called kinematic guidance: The human pilot performs the necessary motions, and sensors transmit those movements to the robot, which copies them. These kinematically guided tasks produce especially valuable training data. Tau’s AI models might not have solved laundry folding yet, but learning from the examples of robots that have completed the task in the real world is how they’ll get there.

But according to Tau cofounder Cornelia Weinzierl, to whom I came clean as a journalist a few weeks after the cleaning, the robot can already complete some other tasks—such as vacuuming and mopping—without any human help. If Tau succeeds in using all the data it is collecting to train truly autonomous cleaning robots, they could even become San Francisco’s newest tech tourist attraction as Waymos become more commonplace countrywide.

The cleaning robot that came to my building last month was already a bit of a spectacle. It arrived in a blue minivan, out of which it was helped by Weinzierl and another Tau employee. That’s when the robot encountered its first obstacle: the eight stairs leading up to the building’s front door. I’d come down to greet Weinzierl and the robot, so I had a front-row seat to its struggles with my steps. It climbed as if it were drunk. Each successful step was as likely as not to be followed by a stumbling backward stagger that erased all its progress—though, impressively, it never entirely lost its footing.

When I later discussed my experience with Weinzierl, she explained that the robot sometimes walks strangely because it is operated remotely from Tau’s headquarters, and the short signal transmission delay can affect its coordination. “The amount of work and time that we spend just optimizing, for example, timings and connectivity is crazy,” she said.

Inside, the carpeted staircase leading up to my apartment defeated the robot entirely, and Weinzierl had to lug it up the last few steps. This, it turned out, was not typical. As the robot cleaned, it repeatedly stalled out, something Weinzierl attributed to it overheating in the unseasonably hot weather—until she heard from one of her colleagues that the heat had shut down not the robot but the equipment that its human controller was using to watch its progress through my apartment. Without remote assistance, the robot couldn’t clean, and so it, and Weinzierl, departed before my booked hour was up. (Back in September, Weinzierl or another Tau representative remained with the robot throughout its visit, but she says that’s no longer necessary.)

You can’t fault Tau on customer service, though. Weinzierl quickly emailed me to apologize, comp the visit, and offer me another on the house (minus whatever price I assign to my data privacy)—and that was all before I told her I was a journalist. I scheduled the next cleaning for about a month later, after a couple of trips out of town, and it went much more smoothly—the robot got up my stairs without much assistance, though still with the drunken stagger.

In the hour it was there, it did a creditable job of cleaning my kitchen (though it didn’t brave the stove) and even saved me my most dreaded cleaning task, the toilet. That was its most impressive performance: Three times the head fell off its toilet cleaning wand, and three times it managed to reattach it by poking around with the handle until it made contact at just the right angle.

The robot is still rough around the edges, which is to be expected for a product in beta. It repeatedly left my taps dripping, it knocked over a (closed) bottle of olive oil, and it couldn’t manage to right an air purifier that it had toppled. But I easily forgave all those missteps because of how charming it was. As I watched it wipe down my countertops, I felt the same fond gratitude that I feel when a Waymo delivers me safely home after a night out.

Still, it’s not all slapstick and whimsy. If Tau Robotics or its competitors succeeds in training robots to clean autonomously and inexpensively, people could lose their livelihoods, and the United States is a long way away from implementing policies to take care of those left unemployed by AI.

But Weinzierl maintains that someday turning over cleaning work to robots could make a lot of sense. “Cleaning is not a job that a lot of people really actively want to be doing—there’s high turnover, there’s a high risk of injury,” she said when we spoke after the cleanings. “We need people, and we don’t have them, and no one wants to do it.” She said that the company is also starting to consider someday deploying the robots for other dangerous or physically challenging jobs, such as mold remediation and home health care.

Tau Robotics still has a long way to go: The amount of data needed to train robots to do the varied and complicated tasks of apartment cleaning is probably enormous, and the company has completed only a couple hundred cleanings so far. But it’s remarkable that there are now humanoid robots able to clean your toilets and mop your floors, even if they need quite a bit of human help to do so. The Jetsons no longer feels quite so far away.

articles.title: HK stocks slip as tech rout spreads to Asian markets
articles.excerpt: Mainland and Hong Kong stocks fell on Friday as a Nasdaq-led tech rout rippled across Asia and fuelled fears the…
articles.fullText:
Mainland and Hong Kong stocks fell on Friday as a Nasdaq-led tech rout rippled across Asia and fuelled fears the AI boom is losing steam, although bargain hunting helped pare losses in markets across the border buoyed by Beijing's market-supporting measures.

In Hong Kong, the benchmark Hang Seng Index ended 315 points, or 1.3 percent, in the red at 24,481 on turnover of HK$247.43 billion but registered a 5.1 percent weekly gain, its best since March 2025.

The tech index fell 76 points, or 1.8 percent, to 4,078 but posted its best weekly gain since February 2025, advancing 8.6 percent, while the China Enterprises Index was 94 points, or 1.1 percent, lower at 8,274.

Up north, the blue-chip CSI 300 Index dropped 1.4 percent but notched up a 1.7 percent gain for the week to snap a 12-week-long losing streak.

The Shanghai Composite Index ended down 40 points, or 1.1 percent, at 3,649 on turnover of 772.63 billion yuan but broke a six-week losing streak to end the week 1.4 percent higher.

The Shenzhen Component Index fell 295 points, or 2.57 percent, to 11,175 on turnover of 885.16 billion yuan while the ChiNext Index dived 101 points, or 3.96 percent, to 2,465 on turnover of 441 billion yuan.

Tech sectors across Asia took a heavy blow after a steep selloff overnight in the United States wiped trillions of dollars off market value, as investors fretted that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections could bring tighter scrutiny of the AI sector.

China's tech-focused Star 50 index and the AI index slumped up to 5.2 percent before paring some losses.

Dong Baozhen, chairman of asset manager Lingtong Shengtai, said the overnight slump in US tech stocks meant the logic behind the AI-driven rally had crumbled.

"The US stock market has been the standard-bearer and backbone of the global AI bull run. Now that backbone has snapped. Can AI bull markets elsewhere hold up on their own?" he said.

Chinese AI hardware stocks with significant exposure to the US market were among the hardest hit. Zhongji Innolight, which makes optical transceivers for data centres and generates most of its revenue in America, slumped 9.2 percent to a one-year low. Rival Eoptolink Technology tanked 7.3 percent.

Jason Hsu, founder and chairman of Rayliant Global Advisors, said China's sentiment-driven stock market was heavily influenced by AI stock performance in the United States.

Technology stocks carry significant weight in China's stock market and "what people are really watching closely is whether AI in the United States is a bubble," he said, adding that any signs of a bubble bursting in the US "obviously will affect the Chinese market".

Still, early panic selling drew in bargain hunters, helping trim losses after Beijing rolled out support measures and reiterated its commitment to preventing systemic risks.

"The series of domestic support measures introduced recently should provide a degree of support within a trading range and help reduce the risk of a systemic downturn," said Ailsa Liao, senior analyst at Forthright Securities.

Some analysts, however, cautioned that the measures might not be enough to insulate the market from external shocks.

"I don't think China can completely escape the fallout from Wall Street, especially with selling this aggressive," said Pepperstone strategist Dilin Wu.

In Tokyo, the Nikkei ended down 3,643 points, or 5.96 percent, at 57,434 for the day and 9.3 percent for the week, its worst in more than six years amid worries new political equations forming in the wake of the US midterms could weigh on AI development. The broader Topix lost 232 points, or 5.9 percent, with all 33 industry sectors sliding.

In Seoul, the Kospi plunged 324 points, or 6.02 percent, to 5,059, a day after dropping 5.3 percent. The South Korean benchmark, down 11.7 percent for the week, has dropped 44 percent from its June peak but is still up 20 percent so far this year. (Agencies)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Former Macao lawmaker jailed 12.5 years
articles.excerpt: Former Macao lawmaker Au Kam-san was jailed for 12-and-a-half years on Friday in the territory's first national security case. That…
articles.fullText:
Former Macao lawmaker Au Kam-san was jailed for 12-and-a-half years on Friday in the territory's first national security case.

That came after the court convicted him on one count of subverting state power, two counts of establishing links with organisations, groups or individuals outside the Macao SAR to endanger national security, and one count of breach of secrecy.

The Court of First Instance said the proceedings carefully assessed all the evidence and found most of the indictment facts proven.

Au did not dispute most of the basic facts and admitted colluding and conspiring with overseas organisations, it said.

The court said he had long personally helped hostile overseas organisations collect, prepare and openly spread political advocacy aimed at subverting state power, as well as false and clearly distorted images and information.

That was done, it said, to stir hatred among Macao residents against the Central People's Government and seek to overthrow the fundamental system under China's Constitution.

On the secrecy charge, Au, as a Legislative Assembly member, leaked secret contents from a closed-door committee meeting in 2021 to an overseas organisation, risking very serious consequences.

The Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office said national security is a red line that must not be crossed.

In an article, it criticised Au for long colluding with external forces under the banners of so-called "democracy" and "freedom" to engage in anti-China, destabilising activities in Macao, seriously endangering national security and harming Macao's prosperity and stability.

It says the judgement forcefully upholds the authority of the rule of law, adding that anyone or any organisation that dares to endanger national security will be severely punished by law.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Peruvian scholar hails Lima-Shanghai shipping link
articles.excerpt: A Peruvian expert on Asian affairs urged Apec member economies to take a page from China when formulating policies to…
articles.fullText:
A Peruvian expert on Asian affairs urged Apec member economies to take a page from China when formulating policies to stimulate the economy, pointing to exports and foreign investment as two key drivers.

World leaders are expected to gather in Shenzhen in the coming days, as the southern Chinese tech hub gets set to host the Apec Economic Leaders' Meeting.

On the eve of the summit, Shenzhen Media Group spoke with Carlos Aquino, an expert on China-Latin America ties who has been involved in Apec matters for years.

The director of the Centre for Asian Studies at Peru's National University of San Marcos also advises his government on Apec proceedings.

In an interview with Shenzhen TV, he explained how scholars like him contribute to the bloc.

"Within Apec, there is an Apec Study Centers Consortium. Every year scholars from Apec economies will meet. We give some ideas to officers, and the officers... apply those policies to the economy," he said.

He said Apec could come in handy for nations looking to grow their economies but unsure about where to start.

"For example in Peru, we have industries, but we don't know how to sell... to a market. So within the Apec framework, we can ask for help – economic help, economic cooperation to the whole economies.

"And we have already asked China, Japan, Korea. They sent an adviser, so they tell us how to produce something, or how to sell to those markets."

Last year, Peru's exports reached a record US$90 billion, up 60 percent from 2021.

More than a third of its exports went to China, its largest trading partner, while the United States ranked second at 11 percent.

"The engine of growth of Asian economy has been trade and investment. And also in Peru, that is happening. So we are learning from Asia that to grow the economy, you have to export and also [bring in] investment."

Ties between China and Peru took a big step forward in 2024, when President Xi Jinping visited Lima and inaugurated the Chancay port, north of the capital.

Aquino said the port, built and owned by Chinese shipping giant Cosco, has cut shipping costs between the two countries by 20 percent.

Other South American countries also stand to benefit, he believed.

"Colombia, Ecuador, Chile can bring the goods to Chancay Port and send [them] to China. So it's having a huge change not only for Peru, but also for the whole of Latin America," Aquino said.

"And you know, we are thinking of building a bi-oceanic railway between Chancay and Brazil. Perhaps if that is the case, Brazilian goods also will go cheaper to China."

He said that, as a result of Chancay, Peruvian exports to China jumped by 39 percent in the first seven months of this year.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Record 400-plus HK firms join Shanghai import expo
articles.excerpt: A record high of more than 400 Hong Kong businesses are taking part in the China International Import Expo in…
articles.fullText:
A record high of more than 400 Hong Kong businesses are taking part in the China International Import Expo in Shanghai hoping to use the event as a launchpad for entry into the mainland market.

Among the first-time exhibitors is a Hong Kong accounting firm, which has seen a 30-percent surge over the past year in mainland clients seeking to expand overseas.

Man Law, CEO of the firm's greater China division, told RTHK that venturing abroad was no longer just a trend, but a practical necessity for managing risks and driving growth.

The expo, he said, is an ideal stage to highlight Hong Kong's role as a springboard for international growth, particularly through tax incentives.

"Suppose you have set up an office and hired staff in Hong Kong," Law said.

"When expanding into Southeast Asia or investing in other foreign markets, you can take advantage of the double taxation avoidance agreements signed between Hong Kong and many countries.

"At their peak, tax savings could exceed 50 percent."

Another first-time exhibitor is a craft brewery that is working up a thirst at the expo for its award-winning, Hong Kong-made beer.

The brewery's marketing director said the brand aims to tap the mainland market, confident that its craft beers will be competitive as many mainland consumers have a strong appetite for Hong Kong products.

The event has also drawn local academic institutions, including the Hong Kong Polytechnic University.

PolyU vice-president Zheng Zijian said the university, which has established 12 research institutes on the mainland over the past three years for incubation programmes, has brought innovation projects such as robots and food technology to the expo.

The institution, he stressed, has benefited from the mainland's comprehensive domestic industrial chain and robust support from local governments.

“Our practice over the past few years is to take the path of deep integration with the mainland and contribute to integration with the country's talent, science and technology, and education,” Zheng said.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Exchange Fund makes HK$18.6bn as tough quarter looms
articles.excerpt: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority said on Friday it chalked up an income of HK$18.6 billion from Exchange Fund investments…
articles.fullText:
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority said on Friday it chalked up an income of HK$18.6 billion from Exchange Fund investments in the third quarter as its chief executive warned of uncertainties in the fourth quarter.

Gains from investments in Hong Kong stocks came in at HK$9.1 billion while the return from bond investments only amounted to HK$300 million.

Investments in other equities contributed HK$1.5 billion while foreign exchange investment brought HK$7.7 billion.

The authority said total investment income in the first three quarters of this year amounted to HK$171.9 billion.

Speaking after attending a meeting of the Legislative Council’s financial affairs panel, authority chief executive Eddie Yue said the fund's performance would continue to fluctuate this quarter, describing it as a “difficult quarter with uncertainties”.

The uncertainties run the gamut from Middle East tensions, financial conditions in major markets, to developments on the artificial intelligence front.

“The US midterm election results have drawn market attention to whether the AI build-out and data-centre construction will slow down, as many states appear to be resistant to it,” Yue pointed out.

“This also contributed to the volatility in the stock market [on Thursday night].”

However, Yue emphasised that the Exchange Fund is a long-term venture and that people should look at its long-term returns rather than focus on short-term results.

The authority, he also stressed, has been maintaining a diversified allocation of assets to make the portfolio more defensive.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: Second domestically built cruise ship set to sail
articles.excerpt: The nation's second domestically-built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, was delivered in Shanghai on Friday. The cruise ship, which…
articles.fullText:
The nation's second domestically-built large cruise ship, Adora Flora City, was delivered in Shanghai on Friday.

The cruise ship, which features distinctive Chinese-style characteristics, is scheduled to launch its inaugural season from the Nansha International Cruise Home Port in Guangzhou.

Adora Flora City was built by Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding, a subsidiary of China State Shipbuilding Corporation, with construction beginning in August 2022.

Compared with China's first domestically-built large cruise ship, Adora Magic City, the overall construction efficiency improved by 20 percent, according to project figures.

The new ship is larger, with more advanced onboard equipment. Its gross tonnage has increased by 6,400 tonnes to 141,900 tonnes, and its total length has increased by 17.4 metres to 341 metres.

It has 2,130 guest cabins and can accommodate 5,232 passengers at full capacity.

Large cruise ships are among the most complex giant system engineering projects in the global industrial system, said Chen Gang, on-site chief commander and chief designer of the country's domestically built large cruise ship project.

Adora Flora City has up to 25 million parts and drives the development of about 1,500 upstream and downstream supporting suppliers, reflecting the country's comprehensive industrial strength and advanced manufacturing level, he added.

After delivery, Adora Flora City will conduct trial voyages and carry out various preparatory tasks before its scheduled maiden voyage. It is due to arrive at the Nansha International Cruise Home Port on November 12, with its inaugural season set to begin 10 days after that. (Xinhua)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: GBA offers limitless opportunities for lawyers: Lam
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Justice Paul Lam has called on legal practitioners from the two SARs to obtain Greater Bay Area (GBA)…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Justice Paul Lam has called on legal practitioners from the two SARs to obtain Greater Bay Area (GBA) practice qualifications to tap into the area's limitless opportunities.

The GBA lawyers’ scheme – which allows those qualified to practise in nine mainland cities – was regularised in September after a six-year pilot run.

Speaking at the Second Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area Lawyers Forum that was held during the Legal Week on Friday, Lam said more than 700 legal practitioners from Hong Kong and Macao have so far obtained the qualification.

“The Greater Bay Area has the characteristic of ‘one country, two systems and three jurisdictions’," he said.

"Greater Bay Area lawyers with dual practice qualifications will serve as pioneers."

Lam noted that the GBA is among the areas with the highest degree of openness and strongest economic vitality in the country.

Hong Kong, he said, will step up the closer interface of rules and laws on the safeguards of the rule of law in the GBA, as laid out in its inaugural five-year plan.

With more than 900 participants attending the event at the Convention and Exhibition Centre in Wan Chai in-person or online, the minister urged them to take the chance to understand the latest GBA developments, grasp new opportunities and expand into new fields.

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: HK, mainland markets feel rumble of Dem AI jitters
articles.excerpt: Mainland and Hong Kong stocks tumbled in early trade on Friday, tracking a global tech rout as fears of tighter…
articles.fullText:
Mainland and Hong Kong stocks tumbled in early trade on Friday, tracking a global tech rout as fears of tighter AI regulation and a slowdown in the sector rattled investors.

The benchmark Hang Seng Index fell 392 points, or 1.58 percent, to 24,404 while the artificial intelligence index was down some 7 percent.

The China enterprises index was down 120 points, or 1.44 percent, at 8,248 while the tech index fell 129 points, or 3.11 percent, to 4,025.

On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index opened down 77 points, or 2.11 percent, at 3,612 while the blue-chip CSI300 Index slipped 1.5 percent.

The Shenzhen Component Index opened down 426 points, or 3.72 percent, at 11,044 while the ChiNext Index opened down 128 points, or 4.99 percent, at 2,438.

Tech led the drop, with startup board Star 50 Index and AI Index both down more than five percent at the open before narrowing some of the losses.

Overnight in the US market, the tech-led Nasdaq notched its deepest one-day drop since "Liberation Day" in April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced sweeping tariffs.

The drop wiped out trillions of dollars in market value on fears of more AI scrutiny after Democrats won big in US midterm elections. (Agencies)

Edited by Aaron Tam

articles.title: US tech sell-off hits stocks in Seoul and Tokyo
articles.excerpt: South Korea's benchmark Kospi stock index plunged more than 8 percent in early trading on Friday, triggering a circuit breaker…
articles.fullText:
South Korea's benchmark Kospi stock index plunged more than 8 percent in early trading on Friday, triggering a circuit breaker as a sell-off led by chip and technology stocks pushed the index below the 5,000-point mark for the first time in nine months.

The Korea Exchange (KRX) activated a 20-minute circuit breaker at 9.03am (0003 GMT), temporarily halting all stock and derivatives trading.

The benchmark Kospi was down around 500 points, or 8.6 percent, at 4,923.47 as of 0026 GMT.

"It is time for correction, but we feel that there may be some overreaction to the outcome of the midterm election," said Jun Kwang-woo, chairman of the Institute for Global Economics, a financial think tank in Seoul,

"Hopefully we will stabilise very soon because after all, we understand that the speed of building AI infrastructure, especially data centres may slow down a bit because of the number of concerns in many states including Texas," said Jun, who is a former chairman of South Korea's National Pension Service.

US stock markets suffered their worst single-day session in more than a year on Thursday, led by a sharp unwind in high-flying technology and semiconductor shares.

Fresh uncertainly over policies on AI and data centres following the sweeping gains for the Democratic Party in the US midterm elections sent shockwaves across hardware and chip suppliers.

Shares in South Korean chipmaker Samsung Electronics fell 10 percent, while peer SK Hynix lost 13 percent.

Among other index heavyweights, battery maker LG Energy Solution slid 4 percent, while Hyundai Motor fell 6.9 percent and sister automaker Kia Corp declined 4 percent.

Japan’s stock benchmark Nikkei tumbled more than 6 percent after trading opened on Friday. (Reuters)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Bournemouth stay perfect in Europa League
articles.excerpt: Bournemouth extended their perfect Europa League record on Thursday as they came from behind to win 3-1 at 10-man Sparta…
articles.fullText:
Bournemouth extended their perfect Europa League record on Thursday as they came from behind to win 3-1 at 10-man Sparta Prague, while Ruben Amorim's AC Milan suffered a third defeat in four matches.

Gambian Ebrima Singhateh ran from his own half to score a fine individual goal as Sparta took the lead in the Czech Republic after Bournemouth midfielder Lewis Cook hit the post with a first-half penalty.

Sparta had Tobias Guddal sent off before half-time and Bournemouth equalised through Tyler Adams on 57 minutes.

Evanilson steered the Cherries ahead nine minutes from time and Rayan bagged a late third as Bournemouth's substitutes fired the newcomers to a fourth successive victory in Europe.

Marco Rose's side have won each of their past seven matches in all competitions ahead of a Premier League trip to Ipswich this weekend.

"It's a big achievement and we have to continue, we need to stay alert, sharp," Rose told TNT Sports.

"It's up to us to use this momentum. Everyone tries to beat us, if we get in a comfort zone just a little bit we get in trouble."

Milan lost 2-0 at home to Ferencvaros as the Hungarians kept pace with Bournemouth, maintaining their 100 percent record in Europe.

Haiti international Lenny Joseph struck twice in the second half at San Siro to earn Ferencvaros a deserved win over the seven-time European champions despite having Bamidele Yusuf sent off.

"We gifted opportunities, made stupid errors. We were not prepared to play football tonight," Amorim told Sky Sport.

"I don't want to lie to my players. We cannot play like this in front of our own fans. It was a very poor performance."

Milan are languishing outside the top 24 with just three points at the halfway stage of the league phase.

"I won't give up on this competition. As long as we're not mathematically out of it, we'll keep fighting," Amorim added.

Benfica top the standings ahead of Bournemouth on goal difference after a 3-1 win at home to Lech Poznan, with Rafa Silva, Gianluca Prestianni and Georgiy Sudakov on the scoresheet for the Portuguese giants.

Bayer Leverkusen dropped their first points as they lost 1-0 at home toa Marseille team that had lost their first three matches.

Crystal Palace snatched a 1-1 draw at home to Hoffenheim as Japanese midfielder Daichi Kamada levelled in stoppage time.

Alexander Prass gave Hoffenheim an early lead at Selhurst Park and Palace lost Adam Wharton to a second yellow card before Kamada rescued a point for Pierre Sage's struggling side.

Palace, last season's Uefa Conference League winners, have five points from four outings in the Europa League but sit in the Premier League's relegation zone, just behind Manchester United on goal difference.

Sunderland, who have more points in Europe than the Premier League, saw their unbeaten Europa League start ended in a 2-0 home loss to Dinamo Zagreb.

Celtic picked up their first points with a thrilling 3-2 win over Besiktas as Camilo Duran came off the bench and netted twice for Martin O'Neill's side in Glasgow.

Teun Koopmeiners and Randal Kolo Muani netted for Juventus in their 2-1 win at AZ Alkmaar, lifting the Italians up to 10 points.

In the Conference League, Brighton edged past Getafe 1-0 in Spain courtesy of a second-half Malick Yalcouye header.

The Seagulls are two points behind the leading quartet of Lugano, Panathinaikos, Twente and Monaco, who have won all three of their games.

Four-time European champions Ajax thrashed Midtjylland 6-1 in Denmark, while Hearts remain without a win after losing 3-1 away to Thun. (AFP)

Edited by Robert Kemp

articles.title: Brutal sell-off for AI stocks sends Wall St reeling
articles.excerpt: A brutal sell-off swept through Wall Street on Thursday, led by stocks tied to the buildout of AI data centres…
articles.fullText:
A brutal sell-off swept through Wall Street on Thursday, led by stocks tied to the buildout of AI data centres. The wipeout more than erased the US stock market’s gain from the day before, which was its best in three months.

The S&P 500 fell 4.4 percent for its worst day since US President Donald Trump shook markets worldwide in April 2025 with his “Liberation Day” tariffs.
