But its future military significance will depend on more than its physical completion, including the extent of Chinese access and the frequency and nature of activities there, Kristanto said.
China already operates military facilities on disputed features in the South China Sea. Ban Keun could extend its overseas presence inland, offering opportunities to build closer ties with the Lao military and gain experience operating from a foreign facility, he said.
The airfield’s immediate military advantages are less clear, analysts said. China has airbases in its own southern territory closer to the South China Sea, raising questions about what additional operations an inland facility in Laos would enable.
Strategic advantage for Beijing?
In satellite imagery of the airfield during its opening, eight aircraft are visible. Private satellite imagery analyst Jacob Bogle told RFA they were K-8, also known as JL-8, light attack and training aircraft.
Chinese JL-8 planes perform maneuvers in southern China's Guangdong province Sept. 28, 2021.
(Noel Celis/AFP) Examining an Oct. 7 image, he identified what he thought was one remaining aircraft, while cautioning that the image was blurry. He suggested the others had likely moved into hangars, although their locations could not be established from that observation.
Bogle also identified what appeared to be workshops and temporary construction infrastructure beside the southern end of the runway.
“So while the runway and main buildings are completed, it looks like there is still some minor work that is being finished,” he said.
The imagery does not establish who owns or operates the aircraft. Both China and Laos operate the K-8 type, according to analysts cited by Reuters.
But a Lao military officer, while downplaying concerns over increased Chinese military presence in Southeast Asia, confirmed to RFA that at least some of the fighter jets at the facility are Chinese.
“It is a pilot training airport. A group of people are envious that Laos has a flight training center, yet Laos has never complained about neighboring countries hosting U.S. air bases,” said the officer on condition of anonymity because he was not authorized to speak on such matters.
“When Laos built Ban Keun Airport for pilot training, some people overreacted. Naturally, Chinese officials brought their own fighter jets, given that it is a joint Lao-Chinese operation,” he said.
Bogle said it was too early to determine China’s future position at Ban Keun, but that the facility warranted monitoring.
This satellite image taken Oct. 7, 2026, shows that previously visible aircraft have likely been moved into their hangars. Next to the southern end of the runway are what looks like workshops and other temporary construction infrastructure.
(RFA) Kristanto said operating combat aircraft from Laos would require substantial investment in fuel storage, maintenance facilities, munitions, air defense and other supporting infrastructure.
“At present, I see little evidence that Ban Keun offers a decisive operational advantage over China’s existing facilities,” he said.
Such limitations do not rule out a broader role in the future. Ban Keun could theoretically support intelligence gathering, surveillance, logistics or forward aircraft deployments if the necessary infrastructure and access arrangements were established, he said.
Surrounding Vietnam?
A sustained Chinese military presence in Laos could add another consideration for neighboring Vietnam, which already faces China across its northern land border and contests Beijing’s claims in the South China Sea.
China’s expansive maritime claims overlap with the exclusive economic zones of Vietnam, the Philippines, Malaysia, Brunei and Indonesia. Vietnam also claims the Paracel and Spratly island groups, where competing sovereignty claims are distinct from disputes over rights to surrounding waters. China controls the Paracels, while several governments occupy features in the Spratlys.
In 2016, an international arbitral tribunal rejected China’s claims to the entire South China Sea based on its controversial nine-dash line, which surrounds the whole sea. This claim was seen to exceed what Beijing could legally claim under the U.N. Convention on the Law of the Sea.
Credit: RFA
Beijing rejected the decision, and has continued to assert its claims over areas that are within the exclusive economic zones of the other claimants.
China has strengthened this position through island-building and military infrastructure, including runways, surveillance equipment and air defenses on occupied reefs. Those facilities support a wider maritime presence in waters where rival claimants seek to protect fishing grounds, energy resources and access to their outposts.
Ban Keun would introduce a different geographic consideration for Hanoi, potentially bringing Chinese military activity to its western side as well.
Bogle argued that facilities in Laos and Cambodia, together with China’s South China Sea bases, had effectively encircled Vietnam.
Kristanto was more cautious. Vietnam would have to account for the possibility of a Chinese military presence beyond its northern border and the South China Sea, he said, but Ban Keun’s inland location and China’s existing airbases limit its immediate operational value.
“For now, I would characterize Ban Keun as a potentially important strategic foothold rather than a major shift in the regional military balance.”
Ream offers a comparison
China’s involvement at Cambodia’s Ream naval base shows why a facility’s use over time can be more revealing than its designation as a joint training center, the analysts said.
China financed an expansion of Ream, on Cambodia’s southern coast, where its joint support and training center opened in April 2025. Cambodia maintains that Chinese personnel and warships are not permanently based there.
An analysis published in May 2025 by the Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative documented Chinese naval vessels rotating through Ream after their initial arrival in December 2023.
Chinese navy vessels are clearly visible at Ream Naval Base, Cambodia. The Chinese navy appears to have kept a near permanent presence at the base ever since December 2023, after the "Chinese pier" was completed.
(RFA) It also found that visiting Japanese and Vietnamese vessels used a different waterfront area from the large pier occupied by Chinese ships, suggesting unequal access to some facilities. Those findings described arrangements at the time and do not establish current access rules.
Kristanto said the comparison with Ban Keun was useful in examining how China could expand its military presence through partnerships that initially fall short of large, permanent bases.
“Rather than immediately establishing large, permanent military bases, Beijing appears to be pursuing arrangements that could provide access, logistical support, and opportunities for a more sustained military presence.”
The differences remain substantial. Ream provides direct access to the sea and can support naval deployments, while Ban Keun’s military utility depends heavily on the aircraft and supporting infrastructure deployed there, he added.
For the Lao facility, subsequent construction and deployments will help establish whether the training partnership develops into a broader operational role.
“Its future significance will depend on the extent of Chinese access, the infrastructure developed, and the frequency and nature of PLA activities there,” Kristanto said.
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Rare photos of Aung San Suu Kyi spark renewed calls for her release
articles.excerpt: Myanmar military releases images of jailed former leader receiving books and letters from Britain’s King Charles.
articles.fullText:
Myanmar’s military-backed government released images of deposed former leader Aung San Suu Kyi receiving items sent by King Charles III of the United Kingdom, a development that brought on renewed calls for the ousted former leader’s release.
Aung San Suu Kyi has been detained since the 2021 military coup that ousted her and the rest of the country’s democratically elected government from power. She was sentenced to 18 years for a broad range of crimes that include corruption and election fraud, though she maintains that she is innocent.
For the duration of her detention, her exact location has not been easy to ascertain.
The military government moved her to house arrest in April, but still have allowed almost no contact with the outside.
Aung San Suu Kyi received an envelope that contained diplomatic communication, and two books from King Charles – “The Land Gardeners: Soil to Table” and “Soil: The ​World at Our Feet.”
The delivery – which the military government revealed in a public statement – lasted only 10 minutes. It is the first acknowledgement of the detained former leader receiving correspondence from abroad.
Family members, Myanmar watchers and world government officials told RFA that they were pleased to know she was allowed to receive the king’s message, but they warned against allowing the military to use the delivery as propaganda.
Kim Aris, the younger son of Aung San Suu Kyi, told RFA that he took comfort that his mother was in the king’s thoughts and that he appreciated the kind gesture.
“I take comfort in knowing that my mother remains in the thoughts of His Majesty King Charles III, and I sincerely appreciate his kind gesture in sending her books. However, we must not allow the military regime to use such selective disclosures to create an illusion of normality or gain international legitimacy. A gesture of kindness should never be used to distract from the continued violation of my mother’s fundamental human rights. My mother, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, is an 81-year-old Nobel Peace Prize laureate who remains unjustly detained on politically motivated charges, hidden from the world and denied direct contact with her family and independent medical assessment. Despite recent developments, we still have no direct communication with her or credible, independently verified information about her health and wellbeing. I hope His Majesty’s thoughtful gesture will also serve as a reminder to world leaders that my mother’s situation remains unresolved. I urge all governments engaging with Min Aung Hlaing to insist on meaningful humanitarian progress, including regular, direct family contact, independent medical access, and her immediate and unconditional release, together with all political prisoners.”
Cara Chittenden, a communications officer at the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office, told RFA that Aung San Suu Kyi should not be in detention.
“The UK continues to condemn the arbitrary detention of Aung San Suu Kyi and calls for her immediate and unconditional release, alongside all those arbitrarily detained in Myanmar. We remain gravely concerned about her continued detention and wellbeing. The UK has also co-sponsored a number of Human Rights Council resolutions on Myanmar, including most recently in March 2026 . The resolution condemned human rights violations against the people of Myanmar, including the Rohingya and other ethnic minorities.”
A spokesperson from the U.S. Department of State said that Washington remained “concerned about all individuals unjustly detained” and continued “to call for their release and the military to engage in genuine dialogue with all opposition groups to end the conflict in Burma. The United States remains steadfast in our support for the people of Burma.”
Aung Myo Kyaw, a spokesperson from the Thailand-based Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, told RFA that the delivery of the books and letters was a positive development.
“However, the world does not view Aung San Suu Kyi as a ‘special prisoner,’ as the regime claims (in its statement); rather, she is recognized as a national leader. Whenever the military junta faces crises on various fronts, they tend to use Daw Aung San Suu Kyi as a hidden political card. In this instance, too, their actions are merely a gesture—a performance intended to project themselves as flexible and big-hearted.”
Kyaw Htwe, an exiled member of the Central Working Committee of Aung San Suu Kyi’s National League for Democracy party, told RFA that the meeting was the military engaging in political theater.
“Engagement should be measured by political progress. When they fail to bring about such political progress, they typically resort to their usual tactic: releasing news regarding our Chairperson, Daw Aung San Suu Kyi, to manipulate the situation. Rather than just sending books or letters, it is necessary to allow her to meet with her family—specifically her younger son—as well as her legal team.”
That legal team is reportedly seeking to meet her in person since May 30 prison-to-private house transfer, sources close to the legal team told RFA. The legal team’s repeated requests to meet with her are ignored by military authorities.
Myint Htwe, a government leader in a part of the country not controlled by the military, said that the junta’s move to publicize the delivery was meant to try to gain legitimacy.
“These are just the same old tactics. The fact that they chose to issue a press statement—when they could have easily handled the matter quietly—suggests a softening of their stance. I interpret this as a deliberate attempt to signal—to put on full display—that they are treating a communication from the British monarch with great seriousness, as a legitimate government would. Furthermore, I see it as an effort to project the image of being a legitimate government to the rest of the world.”
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: Uyghur activists urge Rubio to raise rights concerns with Central Asian officials
articles.excerpt: Uzbekistan trip is a chance to reassert U.S. moral leadership by pressing the C5 to protect Uyghur communities.
articles.fullText:
Uyghur advocates have urged U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to seek commitments not to deport Uyghurs to China and to protect them from Beijing’s transnational repression during his upcoming meetings with Central Asian officials, the leader of a prominent Uyghur rights organization told Radio Free Asia.
Rubio is leading a U.S. delegation of more than 200 business representatives and will arrive in Uzbekistan on Saturday for the first leg of a six-day trip that also includes two stops in India. While in Samarkand, he will attend the C5+1 ministerial meetings – with officials from the five Central Asian countries of Uzbekistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Turkmenistan.
U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio boards a plane, Oct. 8, 2026, in Lisbon.
(Mark Schiefelbein/AP) According to the Washington-based Uyghur Human Rights Project, more than 400,000 Uyghurs live in these Central Asian countries and combined they form the “vast majority” of the Uyghur diaspora outside of East Turkestan, which is the name by which Uyghurs call their homeland, currently under the control of the People’s Republic of China.
As a U.S. senator, Rubio was a champion of Uyghur issues and now as Washington’s top diplomat, he is expected to discuss the safety and rights of Uyghurs with the C5 leaders, Abdureshit Abdulhamit, vice president of the Munich-based World Uyghur Congress, told RFA.
Abdureshit Abdulhamit, vice president of the World Uyghur Congress.
(RFA Illustration) “We urge him to seek clear commitments that no Uyghur will be forcibly returned to China, where they could face persecution, imprisonment or torture,” said Abdureshit. “Uyghurs seeking protection should have access to fair asylum procedures.”
He also urged Rubio to address intimidation and surveillance targeting Uyghur communities, saying people should be able to preserve their culture, discuss detained relatives and communicate abroad without fear.
Communities at risk
Compared to Kazakhstan and Kyrgyzstan, Uyghurs in Uzbekistan face more challenges to their social and cultural rights, Zumretay Erkin, another vice president of the organization, told RFA.
“Uzbekistan is also complicit in deporting Uyghurs to China at the explicit request of the Chinese government,” she said. “Uyghurs are subjected to tight surveillance and transnational repression.”
Zumretay Erkin, vice president of the World Uyghur Congress.
(RFA Illustration) Zumretay said Rubio’s diplomatic visit is a “unique opportunity to raise Uyghur human rights, even in a trade and investment context,” noting that the U.S. government was among the first to take action to address the Uyghur genocide.
Washington classified China’s treatment of Uyghurs in the Uyghur region as genocide in 2021.
Moral leadership
Rubio can show the world that the United States’ moral leadership still matters, Omer Kanat, executive director of the Washington-based Uyghur Human Rights Project, wrote in an opinion piece in The Diplomat.
Kanat cited former U.S. Secretary of State Mike Pompeo’s public calls against returning Uyghurs to China as a precedent. He also pointed to Thailand’s February 2025 deportation of 40 Uyghurs as a warning of the consequences when diplomatic efforts fail.
Omer Kanat, executive director of the Uyghur Human Rights Project.
(RFA Illustration) “This upcoming trip to Central Asia gives Rubio a chance to show that the United States won’t countenance a repeat of that tragedy,” he wrote. “With the right messaging, the trip can fortify China’s neighbors to stand firm against Beijing’s pressure to return Uyghurs to China.”
The WUC also called on Rubio to hear directly from Uyghur representatives and establish follow-up mechanisms for individual cases.
“We would judge the visit by concrete results: stronger protection against deportation, action on cases of harassment and a clear American commitment to follow through after the meetings end,” said Abdureshit.
Edited by Eugene Whong.

articles.title: MPF schemes notice published
articles.excerpt: The Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes (General) (Amendment) Regulation 2025 will come into operation on December 21, following a notice published…
articles.fullText:
The Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes (General) (Amendment) Regulation 2025 will come into operation on December 21, following a notice published today in the Government Gazette.

This commencement notice facilitates the rollout of Phase One of Mandatory Provident Fund (MPF) "Full Portability". Under the Amendment Regulation, employees whose employment began on or after May 1 last year (New EEs) will be permitted to transfer the entirety of their accrued benefits derived from employer mandatory contributions in respect of their current employment.

These funds can be moved from the employer’s chosen MPF scheme to a personal account of an MPF scheme of their own choice. Transfers can be made once every calendar year, or more frequently if permitted by the governing rules of the transferring MPF scheme.

Secretary for Financial Services & the Treasury Christopher Hui stated that with the implementation of Phase One "Full Portability" on December 21, the Government has fulfilled its commitment outlined in the 2026 Policy Address. He noted that this change will give new employees greater control over their MPF benefits, encourage more proactive management of their investments, stimulate market competition, and create room for fee reductions.

Mr Hui added that the Government is currently drafting legislative proposals for Phase Two "Full Portability", which will extend these benefits to the remaining workforce. The corresponding amendment bill is scheduled to be introduced to the Legislative Council by mid-2027.

The commencement notice will be tabled before the Legislative Council next Wednesday for negative vetting.

articles.title: Kindergarten profiles released online
articles.excerpt: The Education Bureau today released the latest online profiles of local kindergartens and childcare centres to help parents make informed…
articles.fullText:
The Education Bureau today released the latest online profiles of local kindergartens and childcare centres to help parents make informed school choices for their children.

The dedicated website provides information on about 930 kindergartens and childcare centres in Hong Kong, including the approved fees for all kindergartens for the 2026-27 academic year. It also identifies kindergartens participating in the kindergarten education scheme.

The profiles display each institution's approved fees after government subsidies are deducted, alongside their official quality review results. Furthermore, parents can access details regarding the professional qualifications of staff and total numbers of teachers.

The website also features enrolment figures, teacher-to-pupil ratios, curriculum information, and reference prices for major education items, application and registration fees.

Additionally, the profiles include dedicated columns outlining the specific support available for non-Chinese speaking students, as well as the resources offered for children with special needs.

articles.title: Human resources meeting held
articles.excerpt: Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki today chaired the seventh meeting of the fourth-term Human Resources Planning Commission, with members acknowledging that…
articles.fullText:
Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki today chaired the seventh meeting of the fourth-term Human Resources Planning Commission, with members acknowledging that the youth unemployment situation warrants attention.

The meeting heard that rising unemployment and the youth employment situation are structural challenges faced by most advanced economies worldwide, Hong Kong being no exception.

Members took note that the Government continues to invest heavily in education and skills training for the local workforce. This includes launching a two-year 30,000 Youth Employment & Internship Programme, as announced in the Policy Address, to facilitate youth employment and development.

The Labour Department will also launch the Youth Employment Link online service portal to facilitate young people's access to employment information and support services. Looking ahead, the continued expansion of the local economy is expected to underpin overall labour market conditions.

The Labour & Welfare Bureau also briefed the meeting on the "Mid-term Update of Manpower Projection" report. Members heard that the Government will continue to promote "AI for All" and support lifelong learning, ensuring that skills in the labour force remain aligned with Hong Kong's future economy.

The bureau will commence a new review of the Talent List soon.

Members said they supported the Government in continuing to closely monitor the labour market and in formulating and refining forward-looking policies on a rolling basis, with a view to maintaining manpower supply in support of economic development, whilst also safeguarding employment priority for local workers.

articles.title: Students share Beijing learnings
articles.excerpt: The Education Bureau held the learning outcomes sharing session of the "Salute to the National Flag" Beijing Visit Delegation at…
articles.fullText:
The Education Bureau held the learning outcomes sharing session of the "Salute to the National Flag" Beijing Visit Delegation at Kowloon Technical School today, promoting the outcomes of the activity among more young people and various sectors of the society.

About 250 student representatives of the delegation from tertiary institutions, secondary and primary schools shared their learning experiences during the five-day visit to Beijing.

Speaking at the session, Chief Secretary Chan Kwok-ki described the delegation as a high-level "walking classroom", which enabled students to feel for themselves the national dignity represented by the national flag and the national anthem through the solemn flag-raising ceremony at Tiananmen Square.

He said that this deepened their understanding of the symbolic meaning of the national flag, and strengthened their sense of national identity and patriotism.

Mr Chan said that students experienced at first hand our country's journey from arduous struggle to the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation from the country's millennia-old cultural heritage to the development achievements of the new era.

He added that the delegation was received in person by Member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and Vice Premier of the State Council Ding Xuexiang, and by the Director of the Hong Kong and Macao Work Office of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the Hong Kong and Macao Affairs Office of the State Council Xia Baolong at the Great Hall of the People.

“Mr Ding conveyed the cordial remarks and exhortations of President Xi and the Central Government to the young people from Hong Kong and Macao, enabling students to feel the care and expectations of the Central Authorities for Hong Kong and Macao young people, and to understand more deeply the important meaning carried by the national flag,” Mr Chan said.

He emphasised that patriotic education has all along been a top priority of the work of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government. Hong Kong's First Five-Year Plan and the 2026 Policy Address also list the promotion of patriotic education as a key task.

He noted that today's learning outcomes sharing session aims to pass on more widely and further what the students learned in Beijing, so that more young people may gain a deeper understanding of the important meaning of the national flag and feel more deeply our country's care and concern for young people.

He said the Government will continue to join hands with various sectors of the society and, through rich and diverse means, enable young people to build a firm sense of national identity, national confidence and a sense of responsibility through first-hand experience.

Today's sharing session began with a flag-raising ceremony. A joint team formed by flag-raising teams of the Association of Hong Kong Flag-guards and the Hong Kong Army Cadets Association, drawing on the experience of exchanges and interaction in Beijing with the People's Liberation Army Ceremonial Escort Battalion, conducted a solemn flag-raising ceremony. Booths were also set up at the session for members of the delegation to introduce their learning experience in Beijing.

Around 1,200 flag-raising team representatives, teachers, students and youth group representatives from Hong Kong and Macao joined the delegation’s thematic activity in Beijing from September 18 to 22.

articles.title: Domestic helper wage up 2.35%
articles.excerpt: The Government announced today that the Minimum Allowable Wage for foreign domestic helpers (FDHs) in Hong Kong will be increased…
articles.fullText:
The Government announced today that the Minimum Allowable Wage for foreign domestic helpers (FDHs) in Hong Kong will be increased by 2.35%, from $5,100 to $5,220 per month.

The new minimum wage level will apply to all FDH contracts signed on or after tomorrow. FDH contracts signed today or earlier at the existing rate will still be processed by the Immigration Department, provided that the applications reach the department no later than October 30.

The Government explained that in reviewing the minimum wage, it had, in accordance with an established mechanism, considered factors including Hong Kong’s general economic performance and labour market conditions over the past year, the city's near-term economic outlook, employer affordability and the basic living needs of FDHs.

The Government also consulted employers and FDHs throughout the review process.

It stated that it decided to adjust the minimum wage level after carefully assessing and balancing the views of all parties, taking into account that this year's socio-economic factors are more favourable than those of last year's review.

The Government also reviewed the food allowance in lieu of free food, and decided that the level should remain unchanged, at no less than $1,236 per month.

articles.title: Five HK universities rank in top 100
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong has five universities among the top 100 in the World University Rankings 2027, published by Times Higher Education…
articles.fullText:
Hong Kong has five universities among the top 100 in the World University Rankings 2027, published by Times Higher Education (THE).

Commenting today, the Education Bureau highlighted that two of the city’s ranked institutions had gained higher positions in the latest rankings.

It said the results demonstrate the robust strengths of Hong Kong’s higher education system and its world-class standing in terms of teaching, research, and international outlook.

It added that the rankings reflect the Government’s investment of resources and its policy support over the years, both of which have laid a solid foundation for the city’s higher education institutions.

In the latest rankings, the University of Hong Kong ranks 33rd globally; the Chinese University ranks 42nd; and the University of Science & Technology ranks 58th. City University and Polytechnic University have risen to 70th and 79th respectively.

The bureau said the consistent high international rankings of Hong Kong’s universities not only reflect the local higher education sector's excellence, but also bear witness to the Government’s proactive leadership in policy measures aimed at driving innovation and change, as well as expanding capacity while enhancing quality.

It added that the Government will continue to spare no effort in promoting the sector's comprehensive integration into overall national development, contributing to China’s development as a leading country in education.

Looking ahead, the bureau said that with the advent of Hong Kong’s First Five-Year Plan, the city’s higher education is ushering in a golden period of development full of promising potential.

“We will continue to promote the all-round connectivity in areas such as talent training, frontier scientific research, and industry-academia-research collaboration, optimise resource allocation, support various institutions in consolidating their existing advantages while pioneering innovation, and nurture more outstanding talent equipped with both international perspective and exceptional capabilities, thereby making greater contributions to the long-term prosperity and stability of Hong Kong and the country.”

articles.title: Nursing workforce planning outlined
articles.excerpt: The Government stated today that public healthcare institutions have consistently prioritised the employment of locally trained personnel when recruiting healthcare…
articles.fullText:
The Government stated today that public healthcare institutions have consistently prioritised the employment of locally trained personnel when recruiting healthcare professionals. The statement was issued in response to public discussions regarding nursing manpower planning in Hong Kong, adding that such discussions should be grounded objective facts and data to foster consensus.

Although the nurse attrition rate within the Hospital Authority has dropped from a peak of 10.9% to 5.4%, approximately 3,200 vacancies remain unfilled with recruitment ongoing. In 2025, around 3,500 of the 4,000 prospective nursing graduates qualified as Registered Nurses (RNs) or Enrolled Nurses (ENs), with about 60% applying for positions within the authority.

These figures demonstrate that graduates diversify into various sectors, including private healthcare institutions, elderly services and rehabilitation, community nursing, insurance and health management. Notably, approximately 99% of applicants who completed the interview or assessment process for RN posts within the authority received an offer of appointment.

As of the end of 2025, over 30,000 of Hong Kong’s 75,000 RNs and ENs were employed within the public healthcare system, representing roughly 40% of the total workforce. Given that nursing practice spans hospitals, primary care, community and elderly services, rehabilitation and other health service sectors, the Government noted that manpower supply and demand must be assessed holistically across the entire market.

Furthermore, approximately 99.8% of RNs serving in the authority are locally trained, confirming that local professionals remain the backbone of public healthcare. The Government affirmed it will continue to promote regional healthcare collaboration and professional exchanges while strictly safeguarding employment priority for locally trained professionals.

Plans are also underway to strengthen manpower training for primary healthcare and advance professional systems to enhance service quality and maximise the professional functions of nurses. Addressing broader roles, the Government stressed that the Health & Care Practitioner (HCP) rank is a dedicated welfare-sector role that should not be confused with ENs due to distinct scopes of practice.

Acknowledging broader recruitment pressures, the Health Bureau noted that private hospitals face similar shortages, with one facility reporting 40 vacancies but receiving only 25 applications over the past year. In response to an ageing population, the Government reiterated its commitment to driving cross-sectoral collaboration and manpower planning based on service needs and manpower data to ensure that healthcare and nursing services in Hong Kong can continue to meet the needs of society.

The Government hopes that all sectors of the community will exchange views on healthcare manpower development and professional training based on facts and data, and work together to foster the sustainable development of the city's healthcare system.

articles.title: SED meets state leader in Beijing
articles.excerpt: Secretary for Education Choi Yuk-lin led the "18th National Day & Professional Exchange Delegation from Hong Kong Education Sector" in…
articles.fullText:
Secretary for Education Choi Yuk-lin led the "18th National Day & Professional Exchange Delegation from Hong Kong Education Sector" in visiting a state leader and Ministry of Education officials in Beijing.

Ms Choi and the delegates were received by Vice-Chairperson of the National People's Congress Standing Committee Tie Ning at the Great Hall of the People this afternoon. They also met and exchanged views with officials from the ministry.

Ms Choi remarked that this year marks the 77th anniversary of the founding of the People's Republic of China, the 105th anniversary of the founding of the Communist Party of China, and the opening year of the National 15th Five-Year Plan.

She said it was highly significant for Hong Kong's education sector to visit Beijing ahead of National Day, on October 1, and to celebrate the motherland's birthday and experience a jubilant festive atmosphere with people in the capital.

Ms Choi highlighted that last week the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government announced its First Five-Year Plan, which aligns with the National 15th Five-Year Plan. She outlined that the Hong Kong's education sector faces multiple tasks, including digital education, talent cultivation and the integration of industry and education.

She said: “The delegation enabled teachers to gain insight into the latest education developments of the country and share experiences with Chinese Mainland teachers in areas such as operation models, curricula and teaching arrangements of schools at all levels.

“It not only broadened their horizons but also fostered exchanges between the education sectors of both places, providing important references for the future development of Hong Kong's education and laying a foundation for deeper collaboration.”

Ms Choi and the delegation subsequently attended a banquet hosted by the Ministry of Education, where they engaged in in-depth discussions regarding professional connections and mutual learning between the education sectors of the two places.

Ms Choi and the delegation members will conclude their visit and return to Hong Kong tomorrow.
